summary: A two-part look at genocide's ancient roots, from a prehistoric massacre in Kenya to Rome's annihilation of Carthage in 146 BCE, urged on by Cato the Elder, and the Asiatic Vespers of 88 BCE.

evidence.note: Nataruk mass grave at Lake Turkana dated to roughly 8000 BCE
Yamnaya / Corded Ware replacement of Globular Amphora people, c. 3000 BCE
long Cato the Elder segment begins: career, Iberia, misogyny, figs speech
extended discussion of Roman slavery after Cato's mass enslavement in Iberia
Cato's senatorial mission to Carthage and his campaign for its destruction
Third Punic War, fall of Carthage in 146 BCE, massacre and enslavement of survivors
Mithridates orders the massacre of Romans and Italians in Asia, 88 BCE
Asiatic Vespers of 88 BCE, the latest ancient case narrated, sets covered end
RTLM and Rwanda used as a comparison on propaganda; theme only, no years

notes: Survey episode anchored on Carthage. Prehistory (Nataruk, Yamnaya) is part of the story per the Part 1 description, not a comparison, so covered starts there: Nataruk is ~8000 BCE but the schema floor is -5000, so clamped. Covered ends at the Asiatic Vespers (88 BCE); Rwanda, the Holocaust and 2022 US rhetoric are comparisons and no longer extend it. Rwanda removed from subjects/setting. Cato arguably co-primary.
